"With a nod, Crazy Ivan leans in closer to you so that you can better examine the many carts clattering about in the lining of his shabby coat.  It's a kind gesture, but his body heat is making you uncomfortable, and at this range you can really smell the borscht on his breath."
!
"Looking closer, you find that most of these are for something called a 'Dendy,' which you don't think Joel's got.  However, further investigation reveals that he has some lovely Sega tapes!  And wow, look at the titles he's got here!  It's all the latest games, which is really crazy considering you thought they'd stopped making those back in like, 1998!"
!
"He's got everything from Call of Duty to Diablo to Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2!  This is great!  With so many options, it'll be hard to pick which ones to get, but you think you'll manage.  Carefully browsing his selection, you come across a cartridge with a rather odd and interesting label; for starters, it looks like the text is in Chinese?  How strange.  You think about getting it, but when you reach for it, Ivan grabs it and raises an eyebrow."
!
"'Oh what the heck,' he says, looking the cart up and down.  'I wouldn't buy this one if I were you, cowboy.  Somehow I get this cheap Chinese bootleg mixed in with my good quality inventory of Sega games.  I'll have to speak with my supplier about this.'"
!
"Oh, phew.  Good thing he caught that; you wouldn't have wanted to get Joel some kinda crappy bootleg game.  Thankfully, the rest of his selection seems to be on the up and up, so you browse through and eventually make your selection.  The trenchcoated salesman seems infinitely pleased that he's made a sale, and he even goes so far as to offer to gift wrap it!"
!
"(His 'gift wrap' appears to be dirty old newspapers, so you politely decline.)"
!
"Having quickly solved the problem of Joel's ruined Christmas, you stick the gift into your inventory and rush straight back into the airport and head back home.  Boy, you can't wait to see the look on his face when he sees THIS bad boy!"

!
"'Oh!  I nearly forgot,' you shout, hopping off the couch and scurrying into the closet to retrieve your precious gift.  'Santa might not have brought you anything, but I got you something REAL special!'"

"'Great,' Joel mumbles, rolling his eyes.  'Is this gonna be as good as that seashell you gave me last year with the office supplies hot glued to it?'"

"'No no, this one I think you're REALLY gonna like!  Come on, open it up!'"
!
"After handing the gift to him, you can barely contain your excitement; you just can't wait to see his face light up when he takes a gander at what you got him.  Apparently still expecting the worst, he rather unceremoniously tears the paper off in one go and tosses it to the side.  Once he glances down at it, however, his face does in fact light up."

"'Holy shit, dude,' he says, staring at the cartridge while stifling his laughter so hard that tears are rolling down his face.  'Where the fuck did you get this?'"

"'From a skeevy Russian man in a smelly trenchcoat.  Why?'"
!
"'Garbagefield,' he says, kneeling down and placing a hand on your shoulder.  'This is just about the second or third best gift I've ever gotten.  Fuck, man, I'm gonna play this right now!'"
!
"And true to his word, Joel rummages through his stuff looking for the Sega Mega Drive he grabbed a while back when he was planning on getting some of those bootleg games he'd streamed in real life.  After a little bit of a search, he pulls it out of the bottom of a box and rushes it over to the TV, quickly setting it up to play."
!
4m
"He slots the game in and turns it on.  As he begins to play, something about it begins to feel... oddly familiar.  But that can't be right, can it?  After all, you'd never heard of this particular game, so how would you ever get the feeling you'd seen it before?"
!
"Then it hits you: the music.  Oh God, the music.  You've heard it before.  You know EXACTLY where you've heard it before.  This is one of... THOSE games."
!
"But Crazy Ivan said this stuff was quality merchandise!  He said it was all on the level!  Did he... did he lie to me??  He seemed so trustworthy, though, what with the stinky coat and the matted hair and the missing teeth and how he was hocking his goods out of the inside of a coat from the shadows outside the airport and... uh.... well, now that you think about it, it kinda DOES seem sketchy, huh?"
!
"Still, he made a fool out of you, and even if Joel is happy with this game, it's not because it's GOOD, but rather because it's BAD.  Stinky poo poo BAD.  And knowing that it's bad makes you awfully mad..."
!
"In fact, you're so full of anger in this moment, that you just can't help but..."

5m

"Well, that was a bit dramatic, don't you think?  Maybe getting ripped off by a stinky weirdo wasn't an ideal situation, but I mean... going all 'HeT' on us doesn't solve anything.  Still, you DID kinda sorta save Christmas, so kudos to you on that one I guess."

"Thy game is over.  You were a level 9 Smurf warden.  You were a devout worshipper of Madrigort, but you forgot to wear your hat to Church last Sunday, so you didn't get to go to the Afterlife of 1,000 Pleasures.  Tough luck, kid."

"As you enter yet another area of haunted forest, you stop dead in your tracks as you notice a tall human figure amidst the trees ahead of you.  Your blood runs cold, fearing for the worst."
!
191i
"Fortunately, it's just that guy from the shitty Unity horror games, Slenderman!  And opposed to his usual silent 'stand at a distance and make you go insane for no reason' schtick, he's casually sauntering right towards you."
!
"'Hey, hold up,' he calls to you in a voice that reminds you of someone's dad.  'I know you're probably really scared but I'm not gonna hurt you!'"
!
"'Don't worry,' you reply.  'I definitely wasn't scared.'"
!
192i
"'Haha, that's the spirit, kid!  Anyhow, hey, I couldn't help but notice you found those eight papers.  The thing is, those are actually some of my important work papers.  Think you could see fit to give them back to me?'"
!
"'Uh, sure, I guess.'  You take the eight pages from your inventory and hand them over.  'I was just picking them up because I thought they were trash.'"
!
"'Oh no, they're very important business papers, and you just did me one hell of a solid!  My boss is a real bastard sometimes and he'd have my head if I lost these.'"
!
"The thin fellow opens his briefcase and puts the papers inside of it, doing his best to flatten them out and store them in whatever the proper order is.  Satisfied, he shuts the case and clicks the locks shut.  Then he extends a bony hand to shake."
!
"'You really saved my ass, cat.  They say one good turn deserves another, so I tell you what: is there anything that Slenderman can do for you?'"
!
193i
"'Stop starring in shitty horror games,' you reply, sighing and turning to walk away."
!
"Slenderman seems a bit taken aback, but as you walk away, you hear him call out, 'Okay, you've got it!  Maybe I HAVE been in a few too many of those over the past decade or so!'"
!
6i
3m
!
7i
"'Oh what the shit,' Joel growls, rubbing his forehead.  'Where are my presents?'"
!
"'Well, Joel,' you stammer, realizing you didn't save Christmas.  'You see, you--'"
!
194i
"'Oh wait,' Joel says, pointing at some gifts that have literally just appeared, swirling in darkness.  'There's some gifts!  Man, I was really worried for a second there.'"
!
"As he grabs the presents from under the tree, you feel like you can hear the distant sounds of white noise coming from somewhere, though you can't figure out where.  The lights seem to flicker slightly."
!
"'Oh shit,' Joel cries in excitement.  'What's this?  I got a whole bunch of video games!  And... they're all about Slenderman?  Fuck, does this mean they're all gonna be flashlight and paper games?'"
!
"Then he takes a closer look at the games."
!
195i
"'Huh, wait... Slenderman and the Temple of the Ancients?  SlenderFighter II Turbo?  Slenderman & Knuckles?  Slenderman Saves Christmas??  These... these aren't crappy horror games??'"
!
"'And hell, the screenshots actually look good!  Man, it looks like that skinny asshole really upped his game!  Shit, this isn't a bad Christmas after all!'"
!
"'Hey, there's even one for you, Garbagefield!'  He hands you an oddly shaped package, wide, tall and very flat.  'What'd YOU get?'"
!
196i
"Tearing off the wrapping, you discover a manila envelope, slightly bulging from whatever's been stuffed inside of it.  Curious, you fold back the butterfly pin and flip the top open, reaching inside to see what you got."
!
"The first thing you grab is a letter, written in a nearly indecipherable chicken scratch.  You'd know this handwriting anywhere: Slenderman wrote this."
!
"'Dear Garbagefield,'"
!
"Okay, kinda weird.  You never told him your name."
!
"'I just thought I'd show you my gratitude by sending a bunch of my new games over for your buddy Joel to play.  Honestly, I can't thank you enough for the advice you gave me.  I guess I never realized how trapped I'd become by all these idiot kids putting me in their crappy Unity games.'"
!
"'Thanks to your advice, I'm now overhauling my entire image with a line of all different sorts of games, trying to put more of a focus on action and adventure and distancing myself from that whole thing with the woods and the flashlights and... well, you know.'"
!
"'Not only that, but I've taken an active role in policing my intellectual property and likeness rights.  You would not BELIEVE how many people were using my image without my permission, putting me in all manner of terrible garbage!  It's no wonder you asked me to take care of it!'"
!
"'And take care of it I did.  Enclosed along with this letter are some photographs to show you what a great job I've been doing.  Anyhow, thanks again for the help!  Sometimes you just don't notice what's gone wrong in your life until somebody has the guts to tell it to you straight!'"
!
"'Sincerely, Ron 'Slenderman' Aaronson'"
!
"Sure enough, the envelope is still very full.  That must be the pictures he sent.  Interested in just what he meant by 'taking care of it,' you dump the envelope out on the coffee table in front of you."
!
"There's... there's a lot here.  Hundreds of pictures.  You pick a handful of them up and start looking through them and... you suddenly feel your stomach tying itself in knots."
!
197i
"Every single photograph here is of Slenderman murdering someone, each one somebody different.  Just picture after picture of Slenderman stabbing, smashing, and otherwise slaughtering kids and teens alike.  In some of them he appears to be posing with his kill, like those tasteless hunter photos you see on dating profiles."
!
"Yeah, you got your wish, Garbagefield, but look at what it cost.  And, despite none of those bodies lying dead by your hand, you can't help but blame yourself.  You unleashed a monster on them, an evil that, while well-spoken and business minded, cannot be stopped.  Even now, who else might he be murdering, all because of you?"
!
"..."

"Merry Christmas!"

Sure, that ad revenue is nice, and yes he's having fun, but he wouldn't bother if it weren't for knowing that there's an audience out there whose lives are just a little bit less terrible thanks to his antics.'"

"While you're searching for relevance, you happen to stumble across a suburban house with the garage door open.  Just inside, it looks like a few young guys are having a jam session.  It's weird... the dude playing the keyboard looks familiar..."

200i
60m
"As you think this to yourself, the power of metal surges through your veins and awakens something within your mind.  All at once, it hits you: that's Glenn Danzig, horrorpunk pioneer and heavy metal legend!"
!
"Of course, it's so obvious now!  The Misfits formed in 1977, right here in New Jersey!  This must be why you had the urge to come here: Joel likes skeletons, Danzig likes skeletons, Joel likes metal, Danzig likes metal..."
!
320i
41m
"You rush into the garage unannounced, prompting the guys to stop playing and stare at you in confusion."
!
"'Hey, what's the big idea,' asks Danzig."
!
"'Glenn Danzig,' you reply, much to everyone present's surprise.  'My name is Garbagefield and I am a cartoon cat from the future!  Your band, the Misfits, is going to be a real big deal!'"
!
"Jerry Only leans over towards Danzig slowly and whispers, 'Uh, Glenn, do you know this guy?'"
!
"Danzig, eyes wide like saucers, just silently shakes his head, staring at you."
!
"'I've got a proposition for you,' you continue, a plan forming in your head as you go along.  'All the good bands these days have a mascot of some sort, yeah?  Let me be yours!'"
!
"'In exchange for being the lovable face of your band, I will provide you with all the information you need to game the system and become EVEN BETTER than you already will!'"
!
"The band's young members sort of glance at each other uncomfortably a moment before Danzig waves at his two pals and they all huddle up, whispering among themselves about what they should do.  You stand there, rocking idly from heel to toe, waiting for them to reach a decision."
!
"Fortunately for you, it doesn't take too long for them to agree on an answer.  Danzig slowly walks over to you and, after staring awkwardly at you for a moment, crouches down to look you in the face."
!
"'You know, cat, you've got a lot of nerve just barging into my garage and shooting your mouth off with a lot of crazy talk about being from the future.'  He casually cracks his knuckles and neck."
!
"'Just because you know my name and know the name of my new band doesn't necessarily prove you're from the future, my man.  None of us have ever seen you before, but you could've just blown into town and started asking around.  Ask the right questions, and you'd get the right answers, yeah?'"
!
"You swallow and nod nervously as he puts a hand on your shoulder with his eyes still locked to yours.  The tension in the air is palpable."
!
"However, you happen to glance up at Jerry and Manny and notice that they're trying very hard to stifle their laughter.  Looking back, you see that Danzig's got a big smile on his face.  The look of terrified confusion on your face proves too much, and the three of them start laughing hysterically."
!
"'I'm just fucking with you, cat,' he laughs, playfully shoving you.  'It's pretty damned unlikely you'd come into town and ask the kind of questions it'd take to the kind of people you'd need to to find out this shit.'"
!
"'And besides, hey, what's it gonna hurt to let some cartoon cat play mascot for our band?  We're the Misfits, you're a scrappy looking guy who I'd bet doesn't really fit in, so hey, a perfect fit, right?'"
!
"'Even if you're bullshitting us with this future stuff, who's it gonna hurt?  Whatever happens is gonna happen.  And hell, if you're NOT?  We're gonna be fuckin' unstoppable!'"
!

"'Fucking great,' Joel mutters to himself as he sees the empty space beneath the Christmas tree.  'No goddamned presents.'"
!
"As he grumbles to himself about the unfairness of it all, there's a knock at the door.  Sighing heavily, assuming that it's more bad news, he makes his way across the apartment and throws the door open."
!
322i
42m
"His face grows pale as he sees who stands on the other side: one of the Night Walkers, with his Skullbuster armed and at the ready."
!
"'You, citizen,' he growls, voice distorted through his skull helmet as they always are.  'Do not fear.  You are in no danger.'"
!
"His words are hardly convincing, but Joel does his best to appear relaxed to make sure the Night Walker thinks he's complying."
!
"'You are to be congratulated.  Our masters have seen fit to personally invite you to their annual holiday show, and you are to be treated as a maximum level VIP.'"
!
3m
"Joel's jaw drops wide open.  This is not what he was expecting; not by a long shot.  Usually this kind of interaction between average folks and the Night Walkers ends with some sort of horrific bloodletting, but this??  THIS IS A DREAM COME TRUE!!"
!
"'Holy shit, are you for real?  What are you waiting for then??  Take me to the show!!'"
!
"The Night Walker escorts Joel out of the building and leads him to one of their armored transports.  As the neighbors watch from their windows, their intense fear transforms into excitement and even jealousy as they realize he's not being executed.  Joel throws the horns with both hands before stepping into the transport, and for a moment he can actually hear their cheers."
!
323i
87m
"Joel's handlers bring him into the venue, and their presence immediately makes him irresistible to the other fans--they can tell he's a VIP.  Dozens of women bat their eyelashes as he walks by, hoping to catch his attention but not his escorts'."
!
"One particularly excited dude makes a break for Joel, hoping upon hope that he'll quickly do something to signal it's okay.  However, he doesn't have the chance, as the Night Walkers take him down in a single blow and execute him with a single Skullbuster shot to the back of the head.  It doesn't matter to Joel, though, because nothing can spoil this day for him."
!
"Finally, they bring Joel to his place of honor in the front row of the venue, dead center of the stage.  They sit down all around him to make sure that no further incidents occur with degenerate lowlifes attempting to approach the masters' chosen."
!
"An alarm blares, signaling the show is about to begin.  Those not yet seated scramble to meet the deadline, dropping their drinks to the ground.  They don't want to be caught not in their proper places.  The last lucky few manage to make it past the blast doors and to their spots as the alarm finally ends."
!
"Then, all at once, the masters' herald appears above the stage, larger than life."
!

!
"Joel is so overwhelmed with joy that he begins to weep openly, which seems to make the Night Walkers uncomfortable but you make sure to signal that it's okay before the show starts."

 "You immediately realize that you are quite literally outgunned here and that there's simply nothing you can possibly do to defend yourself.  Since there's clearly no way for you to fight this thing, you're left with only one option: run like an Olympic track and field medalist and try to find some place safe to hide."
!
"Thankfully, this actually seems to have bought you some time, as only a split second after you make a break for it, a white hot bolt of plasma screams past where you had just been standing.  The creature roars in frustration upon realizing it missed its quarry, and it turns to give chase."
!
"Amazingly, you actually seem to be at an advantage here!  Whereas the thing trying to kill you is large and carrying a lot of weight, you're small and agile and built for speed.  Or, well, as much speed as you can get with those stubby little legs of yours."
!
"At any rate, you miraculously seem to lose him long enough that you're able to sneak through the open window of the town hall's basement.  It's a tight squeeze, but with your ultra-elastic feline skeleton, you easily manage to get through."
!

12m
"Though you seem to have lost that horrible monster man for now, you have a feeling it's not going to be that simple.  Thinking strategically--or, well, as strategically as YOU can manage--you conclude that the basement's not a safe place to hide, as you could be easily cornered here."
!
"Going up to ground level frankly won't do you much better, either.  If it finds you there, it can easily follow you out whatever exit you find, and with its weaponry closing the gap will be laughably easy."
!
"No, you've got to do like the beardy man in that real bad space movie and make sure you have the high ground.  In particular, it might be best to head for the clock tower, since the sound of the mechanical parts operating might be loud enough to mask things such as your hyperventilation of sheer terror."
!
"With a plan in mind, you quietly slink up the basement stairs, through the lobby, and make your way up the stairs to the second floor."
!

"As you're making your way to the clock tower, however, the creature bursts through the town hall's doors, shredding them off their hinges as if they were wet napkins.  It roars in fury, as if it's aware that you're deliberately making this difficult for it."
!
"After looking around for a few moments, it heads for the stairs leading up, seemingly somehow having gotten a fix on you.  Slowly but surely, it makes its way up towards your chosen hiding spot in the clock tower.  Soon enough, it reaches the door and throws it open."
!
145i
"The creature bellows in anger again, making it more clear than ever that it's tired of playing these games with you.  Apparently it didn't plan on you providing this much of a challenge."
!
"Unfortunately, it's still not ready to give up, and it once again takes a long, hard look at the room, as if scanning it for something.  It's not long before the monster once again seems to have gotten a fix on your position, and it follows you once more."
!

"As you're still trying to figure out what to do next, the roof hatch you'd just climbed up moments ago bursts open and your murderous foe leaps out of it, arms above its head and roaring in primal fury.  It's found you at last, and it seems you have nowhere to run."
!
"But you've got one last trick up your sleeve.  You'd hoped to never have to do this, because frankly you're not 100 percent on the physics of it, but you've been left no choice.  You're going to have to leap from the roof and attempt to land on the ground on all fours."
!
"On the one hand, you're a cat, and that's a thing cats can do!  On the other hand, you're a cartoon cat with nonsensical proportions, so who knows what a fall like that's actually going to do to you?"

"Oh, fuck it!  Breaking every bone in your body is still preferable to dying!  You fling yourself off the roof's edge."

"It turns out that in all this commotion you'd forgotten one bit of history you'd read about: this is the exact night that the clock tower was struck by lightning.  And, judging from the bright flash from behind you as you fall, followed by the loudest clap of thunder you've ever heard, you'd guess that now is the exact time."
!
"Being the highest point on the roof at that moment, the creature was basically a living lightning rod.  One billion volts of electricity coursed through it, no doubt doing unimaginable damage to its very cellular structure."
!
"You land with a loud thump on the ground, kind of sort of managing to hit all four of your legs.  It hurts like hell, but amazingly it looks like your cat side won out.  Slowly, painfully arching yourself upright, you look up just in time to see the second surprise."
!
148i
38m
"Guess it must have been carrying explosives with it, and the electricity surging through the monster must have set them off.  If that lightning bolt didn't kill it, you're pretty damned sure that explosion did.  Finally, after what your adrenaline-drunk brain felt like must have been several years of running, you're safe."
!
12m
"However, you've still got a plan to finish, and thankfully now that your head is emptying of 'fight or flight' impulses, you remember that the critical moment has arrived.  Sure enough, as you turn to your left, you spot a pair of headlights in the distance, heading in your direction."
!
"With no time to lose, you rush to the street as fast as your aching body will take you and, standing firmly in the middle of the lane and waving your arms like a lunatic, you flag the vehicle down.  As it comes to a stop, you gesture to the driver to step out."
!
149i
48m
"'Look, uh... cat,' the man says, rubbing his eyes.  'I don't know what this is about, but I'm already having a weird night and I'm really in kind of a hurry.'"
!
"'I'm sorry, I'm sorry,' you reply, gesturing wildly.  'I'll make this quick!  I just need you guys to deliver a telegram to a Joel Jarvisson in Sweden in December of 2019 telling him not to write a drunken, mean-spirited letter to Santa Claus!'"
!
"The man simply stares at you, dumbfounded, as the rain bounces off of his hat and overcoat.  He reaches into his coat, withdraws something sealed in a brown envelope tied with a string, and then stares at that for a moment.  Finally, he sighs very loudly."
!
"'If it were any other night, I'd tell you to beat it, but... okay, look, I'll do this for you.  Just... let me get back in my car to take care of this equally ludicrous delivery, okay?'"
!
"'Oh, no problem!  By all means!  And hey, thank you, mister!  You don't know how much this means to me!'"
!
"The Western Union delivery man kind of just nods as he climbs back into his car and drives away, taking with him the telegram this whole ridiculously convoluted plan was for.  With that piece of information not only safely stored away for delivery but also spookily postmarked from over 60 years ago, Joel's sure to heed the warning!"
!
"And so, having unequivocally saved Christmas, you make your way back to where you'd stashed your time machine, buckle in, and make the mind-bending trip back to the present, knowing full well that all was now right in the world."
!
150i
49m
"Well... it would have been had you known a bit MORE about history.  See, your telegram was written and sent off to Sweden not long after your meeting in 1955.  It was received and put on file by Televerket."
!
"In 1993, Televerket was spun off into several organizations, with the telecommunications arm becoming Telia AB.  The thing is that by the 90s the telegram had pretty much gone entirely the way of the dodo, and so by the year 2002 Telia AB had completely discontinued telegram service."
!
"Joel's warning was never delivered.  Some say it's still out there, hidden in some long forgotten corner of some old Telia AB office complex, collecting dust."
!
"All of that effort was for literally nothing.  Way to go."

"You decide that it would be in your best interest to take the bus to get to the North Pole.  Sure, it might SOUND illogical, or even impossible, but uh... just go with it, okay?  So you head to the nearest bus station, where a crusty looking guy sits behind the ticket counter."
!
"'Where you wanna go, bub?'"
!
"'The North Pole,' you reply.  'And my name's not Bubsy, that's the guy with the exclamation mark shirt.'"
!
"'Yeah, yeah, whatever,' grumbles the ticket man.  He punches in your request and prints you out a ticket.  'You're just in time, #27 should be pulling in any minute now.'"
!
"Sure enough, shortly after you sit down, you see the #27 bus pull up.  You hurry over and climb aboard, handing the driver your ticket.  Huh, that's funny, you seem to be the only one taking the North Pole Express.  Well, whatever the case, you find yourself a seat and sit down."

"You decide that it's important to go to the malt shop for your time travel plans, so you make your way over there.  With a gentle push, you swing the door open, eliciting a friendly jingle from a bell above.  Hearing this, the soda jerk turns to face you with a smile."
!
"'Howdy, stranger,' he says, waving at you with one hand while polishing the countertop with the other.  'Welcome to Joe's!'"
!
"'Oh, hello,' you reply with a smile, making your way to a seat at the counter."
!
"'What can I get for you?'"
!
"The obvious choice is the classic chocolate malt, so you ask for one of those.  He nods and turns to start mixing it up for you."
!
"'So, haven't seen you around here before.  What brings you to our little town?  Passing through on your way to that business convention over in Horton?'"
!
"'Uh, yeah, of course,' you reply, just kinda rolling with the lie to avoid revealing your true purpose.  'I'm a travelling salesman.  From Indiana.'"
!
"'Ah, a hoosier, eh?  I've got an uncle out in Gary!  Nice little town, Gary.'  He slides your drink across the counter to you.  'Anyhow, you're all set.  That'll be 25 cents.'"
!
"Fortunately you just happen to have a quarter, so you hand it to the friendly soda jerk.  He rings the cash register and places it in the drawer.  However, as you reach for your chocolate malt, somebody else grabs it from over your shoulder."

"Turning to face the malt thief, you discover it's a couple of troublemaking teens, or juvenile delinquents as they were so often called during this time!  The one holding your malt smirks in a mean sort of way."
!
"'So, you're a hoosier, eh?  AND a travelling salesman?'"
!
"'Well, yeah,' you reply, slightly confused as to the relevance.  'That's what I said.'"
!
"'Me and my buddy Moose here, see, we got a problem with hoosiers.  And we don't like travellin' salesmen neither!  Ain't that right, Moose?'"
!
"'Yup, yup, that's right,' answers Moose in a rather dimwitted tone.  'We don't likes 'em at all, Rick!'"
!
"'What business do you corn-shuckin' hoosiers got comin' into our neighborhoods and knockin' on our doors, tryin' to sell us stuff we don't need?  Huh, pipsqueak?'"
!
"You swallow nervously.  This conversation appears to be headed somewhere you don't want to be."
!
"'What do you think we ought to do with this no-good door knockin' hoosier, Moose?'"
!
"'Let's rough 'im up,' replies Moose, practically clapping with excitement at the prospect of causing you bodily harm.  'Rough 'im up real good!'"
!
"Thankfully, before they can advance on you, the man at the counter interjects."
!
"'That's quite enough of that,' the soda jerk says, waggling a finger at them over the countertop.  'Now I don't know this fella here, but I know you two young hoodlums!  Moose Hockaday, what would your poor mother say if she knew you were letting little Ricky Pepper here boss you around?'"
!
"Moose gets an embarrassed look on his face and kinda lowers his head to look at his feet as he shuffles them awkwardly."
!
"'And you, Ricky!  I remember when you were only knee high to a grasshopper, and you told me that you wanted to be a doctor when you grew up.  You think you'll make it into medical school if you go around roughing up strangers?  The only place that's gonna get you sent is the slammer, and you know you'd never survive in there!'"
!
"Ricky breaks eye contact and blushes furiously, also clearly embarrassed.  He hesitantly slams your malt back down on the counter, then crosses his arms."

"Moose looks kinda like he wants to add something, but he glances at the man behind the counter and just looks down in shame again."

"'C'mon, Moose, let's get out of here.  My old man wants me to take those pilot's lessons today and we gotta make ourselves scarce if I'm gonna avoid going.'"

"It would probably be fastest to take a plane to the North Pole.  With no time to lose, you hoof it to the nearest airport and make your way to the service counter.  A young woman calls you over to her spot along the desk and you step up in a hurry."
!
"'Hello there,' she says with a smile.  'How may I help you?'"
!
"You tell her that you need to charter a flight because it's fallen upon you to save Christmas."
!
"'My my,' says the ticket girl, her voice so full of saccharine sweetness that you worry she'll give you diabetes.  'It sounds like you're on an important mission!  And where do you have to go to save Christmas?'"
!
"Now that's a good question, actually.  Sure, you could go to the North Pole and intercept the letter, but what if you cut Santa out of the equation altogether and just get Joel something special yourself?  You could go to a foreign land and get him something wonderful!"
!
"So where do you want to go?
"

"Thinking quickly, you pull the can of surstromming from your inventory.  The elves, who were just about to give you the bum's rush, stop momentarily to look at what you've just grabbed.  As you hold it out towards them, they recoil in horror."
!
"'Oh my God,' cries the first elf.  'He's got a can of surstromming!'"
!
"The other elf turns to the first.  'Is he trying to give it to us??'"
!
"'Of course I am,' you say.  'If you let me go, I'll give you this yummy Swedish treat!'"
!
"Without another moment's hesitation, they tackle you to the ground and cuff you with adorable candy cane striped handcuffs.  As the second elf holds you down, the first radios in to dispatch with his walkie talkie."
!
"'Suspect is in custody,' he growls.  'Offered us a wretched can of poison, likely hoping we'd open it and immediately die.  Bringing him in for interrogation now.  Over and out.'"
!
"'You're gonna go up for a long time, cat,' the other elf mutters, looking you dead in the eye as he holds you down.  'Chemical weapons are banned by the Geneva Convention.  You've just committed a war crime, pal!'"
!
"Geez, it's just surstromming, guys.  You'd think it was like, a can of scrapple or something.  Oh well, so you're getting arrested.  At least you didn't get hurt!"
!
"'Alright, get up, you lousy cat.  We're taking you to the interrogation room.'"
!
"'I'm the bad cop,' says the second elf, a smug grin crossing his face as he glances to his partner."
!
"'And I'm the worse cop,' replies the first with a mean-spirited chuckle."
!
"Oh well, so much for not getting hurt.  You probably won't survive the brutal Christmas elf interrogation process, but even if you do, by the time you're tried, convicted, and serve out a sentence for the various charges you're accused of, Christmas will have long since been ruined."
